title: Coherence of the two ordinary scalar models
statement: For a prime $\ell$, finite coefficient extensions $E\to L\to M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an arbitrary scheme $X$, the finite-free ordinary derived scalar models [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition] admit natural isomorphisms to the universal completed-coefficient ordinary derived models [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. These isomorphisms carry the specified completed-scalar comparisons to scalarCompletion [lem-weil-normalized-scalar-completion]. For the identity coefficient embedding such an isomorphism also carries the universal ordinary multiplication to integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarUnit. For a coefficient tower the three isomorphisms can be chosen so that their horizontal composite followed by the universal derived associator [lem-pur-completed-line-tensor-coherence] equals integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp followed by the direct model isomorphism. These are identities of natural transformations on the whole derived category, before imposing completeness or inverting any completion map.

proof.text: Apply the proved pure-tensor and counit-normalized model comparison. Retain its sheaf and derived isomorphisms together with their pure-tensor, cochain-counit and completion identities. The following unit and associator calculations are proved for any sheaf isomorphisms satisfying these tensor formulas, so no transport back to a particular chosen isomorphism is needed.

The ordinary model isomorphism is identity on sheafified pure tensors. Compare its composite with chain multiplication to the prescribed ordinary multiplication using local tensor generation. For associativity, transport the completed-model sheaf associator through the three model isomorphisms. Its formula t tensor (s tensor x) maps to t*j(s) tensor x, so uniqueness identifies it with integralOrdinaryScalarComp. On good complexes, the universal derived counits and the exact-derived factorization comparisons carry this sheaf equality to equality of the derived associators. Naturality moves the model comparisons past the factorization maps; cancellation of the K-flat counit and faithfulness of localization give the natural-transformation equality.

theorem integralScalarOrdinaryModelCoherence (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] :
    (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
      (X : Scheme.{u}),
      ∃ e : integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X ≅
          completedDerivedScalarExtension.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X,
        (e.hom ≫ completedScalarComparison.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X =
          scalarCompletion l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X) ∧
        (e.hom ≫ (CompletedLineTensor.ordinaryUnit l E X).hom =
          (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarUnit l E X).hom)) ∧
    (∀ (E L M : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L] [Field M] [Algebra ℚ_[l] M]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] M] (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L) (j : L →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] M)
      (X : Scheme.{u}),
      ∃ (eEL : integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι X ≅
            completedDerivedScalarExtension.{u, u} l E L ι X)
        (eLM : integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l L M j X ≅
            completedDerivedScalarExtension.{u, u} l L M j X)
        (eEM : integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E M (j.comp ι) X ≅
            completedDerivedScalarExtension.{u, u} l E M (j.comp ι) X),
        (eEL.hom ≫ completedScalarComparison.{u, u} l E L ι X =
          scalarCompletion l E L ι X) ∧
        (eLM.hom ≫ completedScalarComparison.{u, u} l L M j X =
          scalarCompletion l L M j X) ∧
        (eEM.hom ≫ completedScalarComparison.{u, u} l E M (j.comp ι) X =
          scalarCompletion l E M (j.comp ι) X) ∧
        (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι X) eLM ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight eEL (completedDerivedScalarExtension.{u, u} l L M j X) ≪≫
          (CompletedLineTensor.associatorData l E X L ι M j).derived =
          integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι X M j ≪≫ eEM))
